offer.say: Réjean Paquette, Dukes. Equipment. I measure the ice before my players skate. Always. Not because I don't trust you. Because I don't trust anybody. My gun says minus four point eight. What does your log say?

options.text: I'll make sure we agree. Two clean practices.
My log says it's none of your business.
Our numbers are what they are.

why.say: In 2011 a rink told us minus six. It was minus three. We lost a winger to a groin for six weeks. I have measured every sheet since. I have measured my kitchen floor. It is fine.

options.text: Then measure mine. It'll hold up.

cheek.say: Ha. Good. A rink owner with teeth. Will you make the numbers agree, or will I write 'teeth' in my report?

decline.say: Then I will write what they are. The front office reads my notes. They read them twice.

accepted.say: Minus five, minus five and a half for my boys. Hard and fast. And the log. Pencil is fine. Pencil on a string is better.

options.text: Getting the ice to where you want it.

p_rating.say: Close. The north end is warm. You know why? The roof. Every old rink, the roof.

p_practices.say: Coach Rourke said nothing about the ice. From Coach Rourke, nothing is a parade.

complete.say: Your log says minus five point one. My gun says minus five point two. A tenth. I can live with a tenth. I will tell the front office: Millbrook ice is honest. That is the best word I have. Here. A practice puck. Signed by nobody. The best kind.

options.text: Can I borrow the gun sometime?

c_nobody.say: A signed puck is for a shelf. An unsigned puck is for the ice. Shoot it. Then you will know what pro ice feels like from the blade up.

c_gun.say: No. But I will tell you what to buy. The cheap ones lie. Like rinks.

c_honest.say: Good. Most people want 'great'. 'Great' is for programmes. 'Honest' is for equipment managers.

done.say: Minus five point one. I wrote it in ink.
